r.name: Abinger Roughs Nature Walk, North Downs West
r.description: Abinger Roughs has a long history – from the Stone Age to Charles Darwin, the famous naturalist, who walked on the Roughs in the 1870s. Follow in Darwin's footsteps and discover more about the history and wildlife here.

r.name: Abinger Roughs Rhododendron and Bluebell Walk, North Downs West
r.description: Enjoy this gentle walk through the woods of Abinger Roughs, taking in the impressive show of bluebells and rhododendrons as they come to life in spring and early summer. Fairly flat, sandy terrain maintained but uneven paths. Not suitable for wheels.

r.name: Box Hill Happy Valley circular walk, Box Hill
r.description: Circular walk. Dog Friendly, Paths can be slippery in winter, Box Hill, Broadwood's tower folly, Juniper Valley, Happy Valley, Salomons Memorial Viewpoint

r.name: Box Hill Juniper Top circular walk, Box Hill
r.description: Paths can be slippery in winter, Dog friendly, viewpoints, Juniper bottom, Bluebells, Three grand houses, Happy Valley, Natural Play Trail

r.name: Box Hill Train To Stepping Stones Walk, Box Hill
Box Hill Stepping Stones walk, Box Hill
The Box Hill Hike, Box Hill
r.description: Circular walk, dog friendly, steep climbs and steps, paths may be slippery in winter, Please take care with your footing and wear suitable footwear for the conditions, Broadwood's Folly, Mickleham Gallops

r.name: Leith Hill '50 things' Trail, Leith Hill
r.description: Two part family-friendly trail – start around the Rhododendron Wood, then head up Leith Hill, Surrey's 2nd highest. Leith Hill is a great place to learn about nature & for children to tackle the '50 things to do before you’re 11¾'. One steep section.

r.name: Leith Hill Heathland Walk, Leith Hill
r.description: With lots of points of interest along the way, this circular heathland trail takes you through a landscape of heather, bracken, bilberry, pine and birch. Moderately flat terrain with a steep climb back to Leith Hill Tower. Potential for livestock.

r.name: Leith Hill Woodland Walk, Leith Hill
r.description: Enjoy this invigorating circular at Leith Hill, a popular walking & picnic spot since the 19th century. The area around is one of the highest points in SE England & offers great views of the South Downs & to the north, the London skyline. Gradual climb.

r.name: Holmwood Common Family Activitiy Trail, Holmwood Common
r.description: Gentle trail around Holmwood Common with dappled woodland & sunny clearings stretching over 650 acres. A great place to tick off the ‘50 things to do before you’re 11¾’. Signposted & easy to follow with hard, sealed paths suitable all year round.

r.name: Etherley Farm Loop, Leith Hill
r.description: The loop will add an additional 1.5miles to the woodland trail, taking you across a landscape of farmland and parkland. This hour long walk can become very muddy under foot, if wet.

r.name: Polesden Lacey Ranger Run, Polesden Lacey
r.description: A scenic trail run along the waymarked Trust 10 route, taking in Grade II registered parkland & 400 year old SSSI woodland. Find countryside views & nearby Box Hill, Leith Hill & the North Downs Way: all great for on-foot exploration. Steep slopes.

r.name: Surrey Cycleway
r.description: Cycle route consisting of main loop plus link routes

r.name: Abinger Roughs Tree Trail, North Downs West
r.description: Follow this waymarked trail to learn about the wide variety of trees at Abinger Roughs, an area of woodland where you can see a range of specimen trees & enjoy views over the North Downs & the Tillingbourne Valley. Fairly flat terrain with uneven paths.

r.name: Abinger Roughs Snowdrop Walk, North Downs West
r.description: Enjoy this picturesque early spring walk around Abinger Roughs, taking in the special snowdrop trail, with glorious views over the surrounding Surrey countryside. Fairly flat, sandy terrain maintained but uneven paths. Not suitable for wheels.

r.name: Abinger Roughs to Gomshall Walking Circuit, North Downs West
r.description: A fairly strenuous 6.2-mile walk through woodland, farmland, grassland and open countryside, but with the pretty village of Gomshall and its various pubs and tea-rooms en route for an ideal pit-stop and recharge. 1 steep hill & seasonally muddy.

r.name: Ranmore West to Wotton Hatch Pub Walk, North Downs West
r.description: Denbies Hillside & neighbouring Ranmore Common are some of the richest chalk grasslands in SE England. Take in the downs, which tumble towards to the pretty village of Westcott with beautiful views in all directions, plus a lovely country pub en route.

r.name: Waymarked Walk at Ranmore Common, North Downs West
Waymarked Walk at Ranmore Common, North Downs West
Denbies Hillside Nature Walk, North Downs West
r.description: Enjoy this invigorating walk across Denbies Hillside, which takes you along part of the North Downs Way National Trail, across grassy chalkland & through dappled woods. Look out for Belted Galloway grazing, British Bee Orchids and wildlife along the way.

r.name: Denbies Hillside Train Walk, North Downs West
r.description: From Dorking station to Denbies House, then out onto the glorious countryside. The route runs along the North Downs Way & the National Trust Denbies Hillside nature walk; stroll alongside meadows, fields & woodland, drinking in views and wildlife.
